35: //
36: // Implementations should follow the note format described at https://c2sp.org/signed-note, where
37: // the signature returned from Sign is prefixed with the hash of the key used to sign the data.
38: type Signer interface {
39: 	// Name returns the name of the key used to sign.
40: 	Name() string
41: 	// Sign returns the signature over the given message.
42: 	Sign(message []byte) ([]byte, error)
43: }

45: // CheckpointSigner is a function which signs a checkpoint of the log, returning the signed
46: // checkpoint.
47: type CheckpointSigner func(ctx context.Context, cp *Checkpoint) ([]byte, error)
48: 
49: // NewCheckpointSigner returns a CheckpointSigner which formats checkpoints of the log in the
50: // standard tlog checkpoint format (see https://c2sp.org/tlog-checkpoint), and signs them using
51: // the given note signer.
52: func NewCheckpointSigner(origin string, signer Signer) CheckpointSigner {
53: 	return func(ctx context.Context, cp *Checkpoint) ([]byte, error) {
54: 		if signer == nil {
55: 			return nil, errors.New("nil signer")
56: 		}
57: 		if cp == nil {
58: 			return nil, errors.New("nil checkpoint")
59: 		}
60: 		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
61: 			return nil, err
62: 		}
63: 
64: 		msg := formatCheckpoint(origin, cp)
65: 		sig, err := signer.Sign([]byte(msg))
66: 		if err != nil {
67: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to sign checkpoint: %w", err)
68: 		}
69: 		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%s\n— %s %s\n", msg, signer.Name(), base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(sig))), nil
70: 	}
71: }

77: // root hash of the log, each on its own line, terminated by a newline.

35: // Queue is a generic buffered queue for batching up writes to a storage implementation.
36: //
37: // It is intended to be used as a mix-in, allowing storage implementations to batch up

40: 	buf     *buffer.Buffer
41: 	flushFn FlushFunc
42: 
43: 	// inflight contains the entries which are currently in the queue, keyed by their contents.
44: 	// Entries are removed once they have been flushed.

49: // NewQueue returns a new Queue which will flush the entries it contains to flushFn when
50: // either the queue is full (i.e. contains maxSize entries), or when the oldest entry in
51: // the queue has been waiting for at least maxAge.
52: func NewQueue(maxAge time.Duration, maxSize uint, flushFn FlushFunc) *Queue {
53: 	q := &Queue{
54: 		flushFn:  flushFn,
55: 		inflight: make(map[string]*inflightEntry),
56: 	}
57: 	q.buf = buffer.New(
58: 		buffer.WithFlushInterval(maxAge),
59: 		buffer.WithFlusher(buffer.FlusherFunc(q.doFlush)),
60: 		buffer.WithSize(maxSize),
61: 	)
62: 	return q
63: }

66: // the index which will be assigned to the entry as a result of it being flushed.
67: //
68: // If an identical entry is already in-flight in the queue then this is a no-op as far as the
69: // queue contents are concerned, and the IndexFunc returned will return the index which is
70: // assigned to the existing in-flight entry. This de-duplication is best-effort and only
71: // applies to entries which are currently in the queue.
72: func (q *Queue) Add(_ context.Context, e []byte) (IndexFunc, error) {
73: 	item, isNew := q.squashDupes(e)
74: 	indexFunc := item.indexFunc()
75: 	if isNew {
76: 		if err := q.buf.Push(item); err != nil {
77: 			// This does not mean the entry was added to the buffer, so assign the error to

83: }

120: // inflightEntry if the data is already in-flight in the queue, or by creating a new one and
121: // adding it to the set of in-flight entries.
122: //
123: // The returned bool indicates whether the entry is new to the queue, and therefore whether
124: // it needs to be pushed onto the buffer by the caller.
125: func (q *Queue) squashDupes(data []byte) (*inflightEntry, bool) {
126: 	q.mu.Lock()
127: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
128: 
129: 	if e, ok := q.inflight[string(data)]; ok {
130: 		return e, false
131: 	}
132: 	e := newInflightEntry(data)
133: 	q.inflight[string(data)] = e
134: 	return e, true
135: }
136: 
137: // inflightEntry represents an entry which has been added to the queue, but has not yet been
138: // flushed and assigned an index.
139: type inflightEntry struct {
140: 	// entry is the raw data of the queued entry.
141: 	entry []byte
142: 
143: 	// mu protects everything below it.
144: 	mu       sync.Mutex
145: 	assigned bool
146: 	index    uint64
147: 	err      error
148: 	indexChs []chan indexResult
149: }
150: 
151: // newInflightEntry returns a new inflightEntry for the given data.
152: func newInflightEntry(entry []byte) *inflightEntry {
153: 	return &inflightEntry{
154: 		entry: entry,
155: 	}
156: }
157: 
158: // indexResult holds the result of attempting to assign an index to an entry.
159: type indexResult struct {
160: 	index uint64
161: 	err   error
162: }
163: 
164: // indexFunc returns an IndexFunc which will block until the entry has been flushed and an
165: // index assigned (or an error has been encountered), and then return that index or error.
166: //
167: // Each call to indexFunc results in a new IndexFunc which can be safely called by multiple
168: // callers of the queue (e.g. callers of Add which added duplicate entries).
169: func (e *inflightEntry) indexFunc() IndexFunc {
170: 	ch := make(chan indexResult, 1)
171: 	e.mu.Lock()
172: 	if e.assigned {
173: 		// The entry has already been flushed and the result assigned, so make the result
174: 		// immediately available to this caller.
175: 		ch <- indexResult{index: e.index, err: e.err}
176: 	} else {
177: 		e.indexChs = append(e.indexChs, ch)
178: 	}
179: 	e.mu.Unlock()
180: 
181: 	return func() (uint64, error) {
182: 		res := <-ch
183: 		return res.index, res.err
184: 	}
185: }
186: 
187: // assign communicates the given index (or error) to all callers of the IndexFuncs returned
188: // by indexFunc, so that they can stop blocking and return the result.
189: func (e *inflightEntry) assign(index uint64, err error) {
190: 	e.mu.Lock()
191: 	defer e.mu.Unlock()
192: 
193: 	if e.assigned {
194: 		// This entry has already been assigned an index, so don't overwrite the original result.
195: 		return
196: 	}
197: 	e.assigned = true
198: 	e.index = index
199: 	e.err = err
200: 
201: 	res := indexResult{index: index, err: err}
202: 	for _, ch := range e.indexChs {
203: 		ch <- res
204: 	}
205: }

25: // HashTile represents a tile within the Merkle hash tree.
26: // Leaf HashTiles will have a corresponding EntryBundle, where each
27: // entry in the EntryBundle slice hashes to the value at the same
28: // index in the Nodes slice.
29: type HashTile struct {
30: 	// Nodes stores the leaf hash nodes in this tile.
31: 	// Note that only non-ephemeral nodes are stored.
32: 	Nodes [][]byte
33: }
34: 
35: // MarshalText implements encoding/TextMarshaller and writes out an HashTile
36: // instance as sequences of concatenated hashes as specified by the tlog-tiles spec.
37: func (t HashTile) MarshalText() ([]byte, error) {
38: 	r := &bytes.Buffer{}
39: 	for _, n := range t.Nodes {
40: 		if _, err := r.Write(n); err != nil {
41: 			return nil, err
42: 		}
43: 	}
44: 	return r.Bytes(), nil
45: }
46: 
47: // UnmarshalText implements encoding/TextUnmarshaler and reads HashTiles
48: // which are encoded using the tlog-tiles spec.
49: func (t *HashTile) UnmarshalText(raw []byte) error {
50: 	if len(raw)%sha256.Size != 0 {
51: 		return fmt.Errorf("%d is not a multiple of %d", len(raw), sha256.Size)
52: 	}
53: 	nodes := make([][]byte, 0, len(raw)/sha256.Size)
54: 	for index := 0; index < len(raw); index += sha256.Size {
55: 		data := raw[index : index+sha256.Size]
56: 		nodes = append(nodes, data)
57: 	}
58: 	t.Nodes = nodes
59: 	return nil
60: }
61: 
62: // EntryBundle represents a sequence of entries in the log.
63: // These entries correspond to a leaf tile in the hash tree.
64: type EntryBundle struct {
65: 	// Entries stores the leaf entries of the log, in order.
66: 	Entries [][]byte
67: }

69: // MarshalText implements encoding/TextMarshaller and writes out an EntryBundle
70: // instance as sequences of big-endian uint16 length-prefixed log entries,
71: // as specified by the tlog-tiles spec.
72: // TODO(#41): this _may_ need to be changed to support CT
73: func (t EntryBundle) MarshalText() ([]byte, error) {
74: 	r := &bytes.Buffer{}
75: 	sizeBs := make([]byte, 2)
76: 	for _, n := range t.Entries {
77: 		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(sizeBs, uint16(len(n)))
78: 		if _, err := r.Write(sizeBs); err != nil {
79: 			return nil, err
80: 		}
81: 		if _, err := r.Write(n); err != nil {
82: 			return nil, err
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: 	return r.Bytes(), nil
86: }

88: // UnmarshalText implements encoding/TextUnmarshaler and reads EntryBundles
89: // which are encoded using the tlog-tiles spec.
90: func (t *EntryBundle) UnmarshalText(raw []byte) error {
91: 	nodes := make([][]byte, 0, 256)
92: 	for index := 0; index < len(raw); {
93: 		dataIndex := index + 2
94: 		if dataIndex > len(raw) {
95: 			return fmt.Errorf("dangling bytes at byte index %d in data of %d bytes", index, len(raw))
96: 		}
97: 		size := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(raw[index:dataIndex]))
98: 		dataEnd := dataIndex + size
99: 		if dataEnd > len(raw) {
100: 			return fmt.Errorf("require %d bytes from byte index %d, but size is %d", size, dataIndex, len(raw))
101: 		}
102: 		data := raw[dataIndex:dataEnd]
103: 		nodes = append(nodes, data)
104: 		index = dataIndex + size
105: 	}
106: 	t.Entries = nodes

We need to make it easy for load testing tools (like the hammer) to read log contents from the example GCP personality. Currently the example server only handles writes (`POST /add`), so external tools can't read back the tiles and checkpoints that are stored in GCS. 

    The goal is to add a simple HTTP read proxy to `cmd/example-gcp/main.go` that forwards `GET` requests for checkpoints and tile paths to GCS storage. This is only a temporary debugging/testing convenience, so it should be clearly marked as such.

    Specifically:
    - Add a new public method `Get` on the GCP storage type (`storage/gcp/gcp.go`) that retrieves an object from GCS by path.
    - In the example server (`cmd/example-gcp/main.go`), register HTTP handlers that call this `Get` method for `GET /checkpoint` and `GET /tile/` routes, returning the raw bytes with a 200 status on success.
    - On error, return a 400 status with the error message in the response body.

conversation.content:
We need to enable Tessera to support building a [CT Static API](https://c2sp.org/ct-static-api) log personality. There are two key differences from the current tlog-tiles approach that need accommodation:

    1. **Entry bundle formatting differs**: The current `EntryBundle` marshaling uses a big-endian uint16 length-prefix scheme as specified by [tlog-tiles](https://c2sp.org/tlog-tiles). The CT Static API specification instead uses raw, self-describing entry data with no length prefix. We need to support both formats without breaking existing non-CT functionality.

    2. **Entries must know their own index at marshaling time**: For CT, the SCT returned to the submitter contains the entry's sequence number in the log. To maintain RFC6962 compatibility, this index must be embedded in the Merkle leaf itself. This means the leaf data and Merkle leaf hash may not be known until after sequencing has assigned an index.

    The goal is to:
    - Make it hard or impossible to build new transparency log ecosystems that attempt to use these CT-specific patterns outside of the CT ecosystem.
    - Contain changes as close as possible to the personality layer rather than spreading CT-specific logic throughout the core.
    - Ensure non-CT logs don't pay a performance cost because this support exists.
    - Contain changes to the sequencing side, leaving integration concerned only with managing Merkle tree specifics.

    Key architectural changes needed:
    - `Entry` needs an internal function that knows how to serialize itself into bundle format, with the index as a parameter, since the CT-specific format depends on the assigned index.
    - The storage queue's `FlushFunc` must be responsible for calling each entry's bundle marshaling function during sequencing, before integration into the tree.
    - The integration layer (`TreeBuilder.Integrate`) should work with pre-sequenced entries containing both the bundle-formatted data and the leaf hash, rather than raw `Entry` objects.

35: // Queue is a generic buffered queue for batching up writes to a storage implementation.
36: //
37: // It is intended to be used as a mix-in, allowing storage implementations to batch up
38: // calls to their Add method.
39: type Queue struct {
40: 	buf     *buffer.Buffer
41: 	flushFn FlushFunc
42: 
43: 	// inflight contains the entries which are currently in the queue, keyed by their contents.
44: 	// Entries are removed once they have been flushed.
45: 	inflight map[string]*inflightEntry
46: 	mu       sync.Mutex
47: }
48: 
49: // NewQueue returns a new Queue which will flush the entries it contains to flushFn when
50: // either the queue is full (i.e. contains maxSize entries), or when the oldest entry in
51: // the queue has been waiting for at least maxAge.
52: func NewQueue(maxAge time.Duration, maxSize uint, flushFn FlushFunc) *Queue {
53: 	q := &Queue{
54: 		flushFn:  flushFn,
55: 		inflight: make(map[string]*inflightEntry),
56: 	}
57: 	q.buf = buffer.New(
58: 		buffer.WithFlushInterval(maxAge),
59: 		buffer.WithFlusher(buffer.FlusherFunc(q.doFlush)),
60: 		buffer.WithSize(maxSize),
61: 	)
62: 	return q
63: }

65: // Add adds the given entry to the queue and returns an IndexFunc which can be used to obtain
66: // the index which will be assigned to the entry as a result of it being flushed.
67: //
68: // If an identical entry is already in-flight in the queue then this is a no-op as far as the
69: // queue contents are concerned, and the IndexFunc returned will return the index which is
70: // assigned to the existing in-flight entry. This de-duplication is best-effort and only
71: // applies to entries which are currently in the queue.
72: func (q *Queue) Add(_ context.Context, e []byte) (IndexFunc, error) {
73: 	item, isNew := q.squashDupes(e)
74: 	indexFunc := item.indexFunc()
75: 	if isNew {
76: 		if err := q.buf.Push(item); err != nil {
77: 			// This does not mean the entry was added to the buffer, so assign the error to
78: 			// the returned IndexFunc immediately.
79: 			item.assign(0, err)
80: 		}
81: 	}
82: 	return indexFunc, nil
83: }

85: // doFlush is called by the queue's buffer when it needs to flush the entries which are
86: // currently buffered.
87: func (q *Queue) doFlush(items []interface{}) {
88: 	entries := make([][]byte, 0, len(items))
89: 	inflight := make([]*inflightEntry, 0, len(items))
90: 	for _, item := range items {
91: 		e, ok := item.(*inflightEntry)
92: 		if !ok {
93: 			klog.Errorf("Queue: unexpected item of type %T in buffer", item)
94: 			continue
95: 		}
96: 		entries = append(entries, e.entry)
97: 		inflight = append(inflight, e)
98: 	}
99: 
100: 	index, err := q.flushFn(context.Background(), entries)
101: 
102: 	q.mu.Lock()
103: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
104: 
105: 	// Assign sequential indices to the entries, starting with the index assigned to the
106: 	// first entry in the batch. If the flush failed then assign the error to all entries.
107: 	for i, e := range inflight {
108: 		if err != nil {
109: 			e.assign(0, err)
110: 		} else {
111: 			e.assign(index+uint64(i), nil)
112: 		}

114: 		// subsequent adds of the same entry will result in a new entry being created.
115: 		delete(q.inflight, string(e.entry))
116: 	}
117: }

119: // squashDupes returns an inflightEntry for the given data, either by reusing the existing
120: // inflightEntry if the data is already in-flight in the queue, or by creating a new one and
121: // adding it to the set of in-flight entries.
122: //
123: // The returned bool indicates whether the entry is new to the queue, and therefore whether
124: // it needs to be pushed onto the buffer by the caller.
125: func (q *Queue) squashDupes(data []byte) (*inflightEntry, bool) {
126: 	q.mu.Lock()
127: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
128: 
129: 	if e, ok := q.inflight[string(data)]; ok {
130: 		return e, false
131: 	}
132: 	e := newInflightEntry(data)
133: 	q.inflight[string(data)] = e
134: 	return e, true
135: }

138: // flushed and assigned an index.
139: type inflightEntry struct {
140: 	// entry is the raw data of the queued entry.
141: 	entry []byte
142: 
143: 	// mu protects everything below it.
144: 	mu       sync.Mutex
145: 	assigned bool
146: 	index    uint64
147: 	err      error
148: 	indexChs []chan indexResult
149: }

153: 	return &inflightEntry{

155: 	}
156: }

168: // callers of the queue (e.g. callers of Add which added duplicate entries).
169: func (e *inflightEntry) indexFunc() IndexFunc {

171: 	e.mu.Lock()
172: 	if e.assigned {
173: 		// The entry has already been flushed and the result assigned, so make the result
174: 		// immediately available to this caller.
175: 		ch <- indexResult{index: e.index, err: e.err}
176: 	} else {
177: 		e.indexChs = append(e.indexChs, ch)
178: 	}
179: 	e.mu.Unlock()
180: 
181: 	return func() (uint64, error) {
182: 		res := <-ch
183: 		return res.index, res.err
184: 	}
185: }

196: 	}

199: 	e.err = err
200: 
201: 	res := indexResult{index: index, err: err}
202: 	for _, ch := range e.indexChs {
203: 		ch <- res

200: func (s *Storage) getTile(ctx context.Context, level, index, treeSize uint64) (*api.HashTile, error) {
201: 	// Pass an empty rootDir since we don't need this concept in GCS.
202: 	objName := layout.TilePath(level, index)

207: 	if minSize := minImpliedTreeSize(level, index); minSize > treeSize {

25: // HashTile represents a tile within the Merkle hash tree.
26: // Leaf HashTiles will have a corresponding EntryBundle, where each
27: // entry in the EntryBundle slice hashes to the value at the same
28: // index in the Nodes slice.
29: type HashTile struct {
30: 	// Nodes stores the leaf hash nodes in this tile.
31: 	// Note that only non-ephemeral nodes are stored.
32: 	Nodes [][]byte
33: }
34: 
35: // MarshalText implements encoding/TextMarshaller and writes out an HashTile
36: // instance as sequences of concatenated hashes as specified by the tlog-tiles spec.
37: func (t HashTile) MarshalText() ([]byte, error) {
38: 	r := &bytes.Buffer{}
39: 	for _, n := range t.Nodes {
40: 		if _, err := r.Write(n); err != nil {
41: 			return nil, err
42: 		}
43: 	}
44: 	return r.Bytes(), nil
45: }
46: 
47: // UnmarshalText implements encoding/TextUnmarshaler and reads HashTiles
48: // which are encoded using the tlog-tiles spec.
49: func (t *HashTile) UnmarshalText(raw []byte) error {
50: 	if len(raw)%sha256.Size != 0 {
51: 		return fmt.Errorf("%d is not a multiple of %d", len(raw), sha256.Size)
52: 	}
53: 	nodes := make([][]byte, 0, len(raw)/sha256.Size)
54: 	for index := 0; index < len(raw); index += sha256.Size {
55: 		data := raw[index : index+sha256.Size]
56: 		nodes = append(nodes, data)
57: 	}
58: 	t.Nodes = nodes
59: 	return nil
60: }
61: 
62: // EntryBundle represents a sequence of entries in the log.
63: // These entries correspond to a leaf tile in the hash tree.
64: type EntryBundle struct {
65: 	// Entries stores the leaf entries of the log, in order.
66: 	Entries [][]byte
67: }
68: 
69: // MarshalText implements encoding/TextMarshaller and writes out an EntryBundle
70: // instance as sequences of big-endian uint16 length-prefixed log entries,
71: // as specified by the tlog-tiles spec.
72: // TODO(#41): this _may_ need to be changed to support CT
73: func (t EntryBundle) MarshalText() ([]byte, error) {
74: 	r := &bytes.Buffer{}
75: 	sizeBs := make([]byte, 2)
76: 	for _, n := range t.Entries {
77: 		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(sizeBs, uint16(len(n)))
78: 		if _, err := r.Write(sizeBs); err != nil {
79: 			return nil, err
80: 		}
81: 		if _, err := r.Write(n); err != nil {
82: 			return nil, err
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: 	return r.Bytes(), nil
86: }

88: // UnmarshalText implements encoding/TextUnmarshaler and reads EntryBundles
89: // which are encoded using the tlog-tiles spec.
90: func (t *EntryBundle) UnmarshalText(raw []byte) error {
91: 	nodes := make([][]byte, 0, 256)
92: 	for index := 0; index < len(raw); {
93: 		dataIndex := index + 2
94: 		if dataIndex > len(raw) {
95: 			return fmt.Errorf("dangling bytes at byte index %d in data of %d bytes", index, len(raw))
96: 		}

98: 		dataEnd := dataIndex + size
99: 		if dataEnd > len(raw) {
100: 			return fmt.Errorf("require %d bytes from byte index %d, but size is %d", size, dataIndex, len(raw))
101: 		}
102: 		data := raw[dataIndex:dataEnd]
103: 		nodes = append(nodes, data)
104: 		index = dataIndex + size
105: 	}

23: // Sequencer assigns sequence numbers to entries for inclusion in a log, and provides a way for
24: // those sequenced entries to be consumed by the log.
25: //
26: // Implementations must be able to cope with multiple concurrent calls to AssignEntries, and must
27: // ensure that each entry is assigned a unique sequence number. The sequence numbers given to the
28: // entries passed to a single call to AssignEntries are consecutive, and in the same order as the
29: // entries given.
30: //
31: // AssignEntries and ConsumeEntries may be called concurrently with each other, but an entry is
32: // only ever handed to a single call to ConsumeEntries.
33: type Sequencer interface {
34: 	// AssignEntries assigns sequence numbers to the given entries, and returns the sequence
35: 	// numbers which were assigned to them, in the same order as the entries given.
36: 	//
37: 	// Upon success, the entries are considered to have been sequenced, and will be made
38: 	// available to future calls to ConsumeEntries. If an error is returned, then none of the
39: 	// entries should be considered to have been assigned sequence numbers.
40: 	AssignEntries(ctx context.Context, entries []*tessera.Entry) ([]uint64, error)
41: 
42: 	// ConsumeEntries retrieves batches of sequenced entries which have not yet been consumed, and
43: 	// calls the provided function f for each of those batches, in the order in which they were
44: 	// sequenced.
45: 	//
46: 	// A batch is only marked as consumed once f has been called with it and has returned without
47: 	// error; batches for which f returns an error are left unconsumed, and will be handed to f
48: 	// again by a future call to ConsumeEntries.
49: 	//
50: 	// ConsumeEntries returns once every currently-sequenced batch has been consumed, or an error
51: 	// (either from the underlying storage, or from f) is encountered, in which case that error is
52: 	// returned.
53: 	ConsumeEntries(ctx context.Context, f func(entries []*tessera.Entry) error) error
54: }

52: // sequence numbers, starting from the next available sequence number.
53: // The batch is then made available to be consumed by future calls to ConsumeEntries.
54: func (s *Storage) AssignEntries(ctx context.Context, entries []*tessera.Entry) ([]uint64, error) {
55: 	if len(entries) == 0 {

65: 	bundle := &api.EntryBundle{Entries: make([][]byte, 0, len(entries))}
66: 	assigned := make([]uint64, 0, len(entries))
67: 	for i, e := range entries {
68: 		bundle.Entries = append(bundle.Entries, e.Data())
69: 		assigned = append(assigned, next+uint64(i))
70: 	}
71: 	bundleBytes, err := bundle.MarshalText()
72: 	if err != nil {
73: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal entry batch: %w", err)
74: 	}
75: 
76: 	batches = append(batches, sequencerBatch{index: next, bundle: bundleBytes})
77: 	if err := s.writeSequencerState(ctx, next+uint64(len(entries)), batches); err != nil {
78: 		return nil, err
79: 	}
80: 	return assigned, nil
81: }
82: 
83: // ConsumeEntries implements the storage.Sequencer interface.
84: //
85: // Sequenced entries are passed to f, one batch at a time, in the order in which they were
86: // sequenced. A batch is only marked as consumed once f has returned without error; if f returns an
87: // error then the batch (and any subsequent batches) are left unconsumed, and will be handed to f
88: // again by a future call to ConsumeEntries.
89: func (s *Storage) ConsumeEntries(ctx context.Context, f func(entries []*tessera.Entry) error) error {
90: 	next, batches, err := s.readSequencerState(ctx)
91: 	if err != nil {
92: 		return err
93: 	}
94: 	if len(batches) == 0 {
95: 		return nil
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	unconsumed := make([]sequencerBatch, 0, len(batches))
99: 	for i, b := range batches {
100: 		// Unmarshal the batch's entries.
101: 		bundle := &api.EntryBundle{}
102: 		if err := bundle.UnmarshalText(b.bundle); err != nil {
103: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal entry batch at seq %d: %w", b.index, err)
104: 		}
105: 		entries := make([]*tessera.Entry, 0, len(bundle.Entries))
106: 		for _, data := range bundle.Entries {
107: 			e := tessera.NewEntry(data)
108: 			entries = append(entries, &e)
109: 		}
110: 
111: 		if err := f(entries); err != nil {
112: 			// The batch was not consumed, so leave it (and all subsequent batches) in the
113: 			// state to be consumed by a future call.
114: 			unconsumed = append(unconsumed, b)
115: 			unconsumed = append(unconsumed, batches[i+1:]...)
116: 			if werr := s.writeSequencerState(ctx, next, unconsumed); werr != nil {
117: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to persist sequencer state after callback error: %w", werr)
118: 			}
119: 			return err
120: 		}
121: 		// The batch was successfully consumed; it is omitted from the state written below.
122: 	}
123: 
124: 	if err := s.writeSequencerState(ctx, next, nil); err != nil {
125: 		return err
126: 	}
127: 	return nil
128: }
129: 
130: // StartConsumerLoop runs a background loop which periodically consumes sequenced entries which are
131: // waiting to be consumed, passing them to f.
132: //
133: // The loop will consume any sequenced entries which are waiting to be consumed as soon as it
134: // starts, and will check for newly sequenced entries at the given interval thereafter.
135: //
136: // StartConsumerLoop blocks until ctx is done, at which point it will return ctx.Err().
137: func (s *Storage) StartConsumerLoop(ctx context.Context, interval time.Duration, f func(entries []*tessera.Entry) error) error {
138: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
139: 	defer ticker.Stop()
140: 	for {
141: 		if err := s.ConsumeEntries(ctx, f); err != nil {
142: 			if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
143: 				klog.Errorf("Failed to consume sequenced entries: %v", err)
144: 			}
145: 		}
146: 		select {
147: 		case <-ctx.Done():
148: 			return ctx.Err()
149: 		case <-ticker.C:
150: 		}
151: 	}
152: }
153: 
154: // readSequencerState reads and decodes the sequencer state object, or returns an empty state (with
155: // a next sequence number of 0) if no state has been persisted yet.
156: func (s *Storage) readSequencerState(ctx context.Context) (uint64, []sequencerBatch, error) {
157: 	data, _, err := s.objStore.getObject(ctx, sequencerStatePath)
158: 	if err != nil {
159: 		if errors.Is(err, gcs.ErrObjectNotExist) {
160: 			// No state has been persisted yet, so the sequencer is starting from scratch.
161: 			return 0, nil, nil
162: 		}
163: 		return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read sequencer state: %w", err)
164: 	}
165: 	next, batches, err := unmarshalSequencerState(data)
166: 	if err != nil {
167: 		return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode sequencer state: %w", err)
168: 	}
169: 	return next, batches, nil
170: }
171: 
172: // writeSequencerState encodes the given sequencer state and persists it to the object store.
173: func (s *Storage) writeSequencerState(ctx context.Context, next uint64, batches []sequencerBatch) error {
174: 	if err := s.objStore.setObject(ctx, sequencerStatePath, marshalSequencerState(next, batches), nil); err != nil {
175: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write sequencer state: %w", err)
176: 	}
177: 	return nil
178: }
179: 
180: // marshalSequencerState encodes the sequencer state as a big-endian sequence of uint64 values, with
181: // the contents of each batch's entry bundle appended verbatim:
182: //
183: //	[next sequence number][num batches]([first seq of batch][bundle byte length][bundle bytes])...
184: func marshalSequencerState(next uint64, batches []sequencerBatch) []byte {
185: 	var buf bytes.Buffer
186: 	write := func(v uint64) {
187: 		var b [8]byte
188: 		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b[:], v)
189: 		buf.Write(b[:])
190: 	}
191: 	write(next)
192: 	write(uint64(len(batches)))
193: 	for _, b := range batches {
194: 		write(b.index)
195: 		write(uint64(len(b.bundle)))
196: 		buf.Write(b.bundle)
197: 	}
198: 	return buf.Bytes()
199: }
200: 
201: // unmarshalSequencerState decodes the byte representation of the sequencer state produced by
202: // marshalSequencerState.
203: func unmarshalSequencerState(data []byte) (uint64, []sequencerBatch, error) {
204: 	if len(data) < 16 {
205: 		return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("sequencer state of %d bytes is too short", len(data))
206: 	}
207: 	next := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[:8])
208: 	numBatches := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[8:16])
209: 	batches := make([]sequencerBatch, 0, numBatches)
210: 	offset := 16
211: 	for i := uint64(0); i < numBatches; i++ {
212: 		if len(data)-offset < 16 {
213: 			return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("sequencer state truncated in the header of batch %d", i)
214: 		}
215: 		index := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[offset : offset+8])
216: 		bundleLen := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[offset+8 : offset+16])
217: 		offset += 16
218: 		if uint64(len(data)-offset) < bundleLen {
219: 			return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("sequencer state truncated in the data of batch %d", i)
220: 		}
221: 		batches = append(batches, sequencerBatch{index: index, bundle: data[offset : offset+int(bundleLen)]})
222: 		offset += int(bundleLen)
223: 	}
224: 	return next, batches, nil
225: }

16: 
17: import (
18: 	"context"
19: 	"encoding/base64"
20: 	"errors"
21: 	"fmt"
22: )
23: 
24: // Checkpoint represents the log at a given moment in time.
25: //
26: // Checkpoints enable clients to verify the consistency of the log.
27: type Checkpoint struct {
28: 	// Size is the number of entries which the log contains at the time the checkpoint was created.
29: 	Size uint64
30: 	// Hash is the root hash of the log at the time the checkpoint was created.
31: 	Hash []byte
32: }
33: 
34: // Signer is the interface which must be implemented by note signers used to sign checkpoints.
35: //
36: // Implementations should follow the note format described at https://c2sp.org/signed-note, where
37: // the signature returned from Sign is prefixed with the hash of the key used to sign the data.
38: type Signer interface {
39: 	// Name returns the name of the key used to sign.
40: 	Name() string
41: 	// Sign returns the signature over the given message.
42: 	Sign(message []byte) ([]byte, error)
43: }
44: 
45: // CheckpointSigner is a function which signs a checkpoint of the log, returning the signed
46: // checkpoint.
47: type CheckpointSigner func(ctx context.Context, cp *Checkpoint) ([]byte, error)
48: 
49: // NewCheckpointSigner returns a CheckpointSigner which formats checkpoints of the log in the
50: // standard tlog checkpoint format (see https://c2sp.org/tlog-checkpoint), and signs them using
51: // the given note signer.
52: func NewCheckpointSigner(origin string, signer Signer) CheckpointSigner {
53: 	return func(ctx context.Context, cp *Checkpoint) ([]byte, error) {
54: 		if signer == nil {
55: 			return nil, errors.New("nil signer")
56: 		}
57: 		if cp == nil {
58: 			return nil, errors.New("nil checkpoint")
59: 		}
60: 		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
61: 			return nil, err
62: 		}
63: 
64: 		msg := formatCheckpoint(origin, cp)
65: 		sig, err := signer.Sign([]byte(msg))
66: 		if err != nil {
67: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to sign checkpoint: %w", err)
68: 		}
69: 		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%s\n— %s %s\n", msg, signer.Name(), base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(sig))), nil
70: 	}
71: }
72: 
73: // formatCheckpoint returns the standard tlog checkpoint representation of the given checkpoint,
74: // prefixed with the given origin.
75: //
76: // The checkpoint is the origin, the size of the log, and the base64 (unpadded) encoding of the
77: // root hash of the log, each on its own line, terminated by a newline.
78: func formatCheckpoint(origin string, cp *Checkpoint) string {
79: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s\n%d\n%s\n", origin, cp.Size, base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(cp.Hash))
80: }

27: // PartialTileSize returns the expected number of leaves in a tile at the given location within
28: // a tree of the specified logSize, or 0 if the tile is expected to be fully populated.
29: func PartialTileSize(level, index, logSize uint64) uint64 {
30: 	sizeAtLevel := logSize >> (level * 8)
31: 	fullTiles := sizeAtLevel / 256
32: 	if index < fullTiles {
33: 		return 0
34: 	}
35: 	return sizeAtLevel % 256
36: }

38: // NodeCoordsToTileAddress returns the (TileLevel, TileIndex) in tile-space, and the
39: // (NodeLevel, NodeIndex) address within that tile of the specified tree node co-ordinates.
40: func NodeCoordsToTileAddress(treeLevel, treeIndex uint64) (uint64, uint64, uint, uint64) {
41: 	tileRowWidth := uint64(1 << (8 - treeLevel%8))
42: 	tileLevel := treeLevel / 8
43: 	tileIndex := treeIndex / tileRowWidth
44: 	nodeLevel := uint(treeLevel % 8)
45: 	nodeIndex := uint64(treeIndex % tileRowWidth)
46: 
47: 	return tileLevel, tileIndex, nodeLevel, nodeIndex

15: // Package layout contains routines for specifying the path layout of Tessera logs,
16: // which is really to say that it provides functions to calculate paths used by the
17: // tlog-tiles API: https://github.com/C2SP/C2SP/blob/main/tlog-tiles.md
18: package layout
19: 
20: import (
21: 	"fmt"
22: )
23: 
24: const (
25: 	// CheckpointPath is the location of the file containing the log checkpoint.
26: 	CheckpointPath = "checkpoint"
27: )
28: 
29: // EntriesPathForLogIndex builds the local path at which the leaf with the given index lives in.
30: // Note that this will be an entry bundle containing up to 256 entries and thus multiple
31: // indices can map to the same output path.
32: //
33: // TODO(mhutchinson): revisit to consider how partial tile suffixes should be added.
34: func EntriesPathForLogIndex(seq uint64) string {
35: 	return EntriesPath(seq / 256)
36: }
37: 
38: // EntriesPath returns the local path for the Nth entry bundle.
39: func EntriesPath(N uint64) string {
40: 	return fmt.Sprintf("tile/entries%s", fmtN(N))
41: }
42: 
43: // TilePath builds the path to the subtree tile with the given level and index in tile space.
44: func TilePath(tileLevel, tileIndex uint64) string {
45: 	return fmt.Sprintf("tile/%d%s", tileLevel, fmtN(tileIndex))
46: }
47: 
48: // fmtN returns the "N" part of a Tiles-spec path.
49: //
50: // N is grouped into chunks of 3 decimal digits, starting with the most significant digit, and
51: // padding with zeroes as necessary.
52: // Digit groups are prefixed with "x", except for the least-significant group which has no prefix,
53: // and separated with slashes.
54: //
55: // See https://github.com/C2SP/C2SP/blob/main/tlog-tiles.md#:~:text=index%201234067%20will%20be%20encoded%20as%20x001/x234/067
56: func fmtN(N uint64) string {
57: 	n := fmt.Sprintf("/%03d", N%1000)
58: 	N /= 1000
59: 	for N > 0 {
60: 		n = fmt.Sprintf("/x%03d%s", N%1000, n)
61: 		N /= 1000
62: 	}
63: 	return n
64: }

15: // Package mysql contains a MySQL-based storage implementation for Tessera.
16: package mysql
17: 
18: import (

20: 	"crypto/sha256"

28: 	"k8s.io/klog/v2"
29: )
30: 
31: const (
32: 	selectCheckpointByIDSQL = "SELECT `note` FROM `Checkpoint` WHERE `id` = ?"
33: 	replaceCheckpointSQL    = "REPLACE INTO `Checkpoint` (`id`, `note`) VALUES (?, ?)"
34: 
35: 	selectSubtreeByTileIDSQL = "SELECT `data` FROM `Subtree` WHERE `tile_id` = ?"
36: 
37: 	checkpointID = 0
38: )
39: 
40: // Storage is a MySQL-based storage implementation for Tessera.
41: type Storage struct {
42: 	db *sql.DB
43: }
44: 
45: // New creates a new instance of the MySQL-based Storage.
46: func New(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) (*Storage, error) {
47: 	s := &Storage{
48: 		db: db,
49: 	}
50: 	if err := s.db.Ping(); err != nil {
51: 		klog.Errorf("Failed to ping database: %v", err)
52: 		return nil, err
53: 	}
54: 
55: 	// Initialize checkpoint if there is no row in the Checkpoint table.
56: 	if _, err := s.ReadCheckpoint(ctx); err != nil {
57: 		if err != sql.ErrNoRows {
58: 			klog.Errorf("Failed to read checkpoint: %v", err)
59: 			return nil, err
60: 		}
61: 
62: 		klog.Infof("Initializing checkpoint")
63: 		if err := s.writeCheckpoint(ctx, []byte("")); err != nil {
64: 			klog.Errorf("Failed to write initial checkpoint: %v", err)
65: 			return nil, err
66: 		}
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	return s, nil
70: }
71: 
72: // ReadCheckpoint returns the latest stored checkpoint.
73: func (s *Storage) ReadCheckpoint(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error) {
74: 	row := s.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, selectCheckpointByIDSQL, checkpointID)
75: 	if err := row.Err(); err != nil {
76: 		return nil, err
77: 	}
78: 
79: 	var checkpoint []byte
80: 	return checkpoint, row.Scan(&checkpoint)
81: }
82: 
83: // writeCheckpoint stores a raw log checkpoint.
84: func (s *Storage) writeCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, rawCheckpoint []byte) error {
85: 	// Get a Tx for making transaction requests.
86: 	tx, err := s.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
87: 	if err != nil {
88: 		return err
89: 	}
90: 	// Defer a rollback in case anything fails.
91: 	defer func() {
92: 		if err := tx.Rollback(); err != nil && err != sql.ErrTxDone {
93: 			klog.Errorf("Failed to rollback in writeCheckpoint: %v", err)
94: 		}
95: 	}()
96: 
97: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, replaceCheckpointSQL, checkpointID, rawCheckpoint); err != nil {
98: 		klog.Errorf("Failed to execute replaceCheckpointSQL: %v", err)
99: 		return err
100: 	}
101: 
102: 	// Commit the transaction.
103: 	return tx.Commit()
104: }
105: 
106: // ReadTile reads the tile at the given level and index, and returns the first width hashes in the tile.
107: //
108: // If the stored tile contains fewer than width hashes then the whole tile is returned.
109: func (s *Storage) ReadTile(ctx context.Context, level, index, width uint64) ([][]byte, error) {
110: 	tile, err := s.getTile(ctx, level, index)
111: 	if err != nil {
112: 		return nil, err
113: 	}
114: 	if uint64(len(tile)) > width {
115: 		return tile[:width], nil
116: 	}
117: 	return tile, nil
118: }
119: 
120: // getTile returns the stored tile at the given level and index, or os.ErrNotExist if it doesn't exist.
121: func (s *Storage) getTile(ctx context.Context, level, index uint64) ([][]byte, error) {
122: 	var data []byte
123: 	if err := s.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, selectSubtreeByTileIDSQL, layout.TileID(level, index)).Scan(&data); err != nil {
124: 		if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
125: 			return nil, os.ErrNotExist
126: 		}
127: 		return nil, err
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	// Recreate the tile slices.
131: 	l := len(data)
132: 	if m := l % sha256.Size; m != 0 {
133: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid tile data size %d", l)
134: 	}

15: // Package compact provides compact Merkle tree data structures.
16: package compact
17: 
18: import (
19: 	"bytes"
20: 	"errors"
21: 	"fmt"
22: 	"math/bits"
23: )
24: 
25: // HashFn computes an internal node's hash using the hashes of its child nodes.
26: type HashFn func(left, right []byte) []byte
27: 
28: // VisitFn visits the node with the specified ID and hash.
29: type VisitFn func(id NodeID, hash []byte)
30: 
31: // RangeFactory allows creating compact ranges with the specified hash
32: // function, which must not be nil, and must not be changed.
33: type RangeFactory struct {
34: 	Hash HashFn
35: }
36: 
37: // NewRange creates a Range for [begin, end) with the given set of hashes. The
38: // hashes correspond to the roots of the minimal set of perfect sub-trees
39: // covering the [begin, end) leaves range, ordered left to right.
40: func (f *RangeFactory) NewRange(begin, end uint64, hashes [][]byte) (*Range, error) {
41: 	if end < begin {
42: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid range: end=%d, want >= %d", end, begin)
43: 	}
44: 	if got, want := len(hashes), RangeSize(begin, end); got != want {
45: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid hashes: got %d values, want %d", got, want)
46: 	}
47: 	return &Range{f: f, begin: begin, end: end, hashes: hashes}, nil
48: }
49: 
50: // NewEmptyRange returns a new Range for an empty [begin, begin) range. The
51: // value of begin defines where the range will start growing from when entries
52: // are appended to it.
53: func (f *RangeFactory) NewEmptyRange(begin uint64) *Range {
54: 	return &Range{f: f, begin: begin, end: begin}
55: }
56: 
57: // Range represents a compact Merkle tree range for leaf indices [begin, end).
58: //
59: // It contains the minimal set of perfect subtrees whose leaves comprise this
60: // range. The structure is efficiently mergeable with other compact ranges that
61: // share one of the endpoints with it.
62: //
63: // For more details, see
64: // https://github.com/transparency-dev/merkle/blob/main/docs/compact_ranges.md.
65: type Range struct {
66: 	f      *RangeFactory
67: 	begin  uint64
68: 	end    uint64
69: 	hashes [][]byte
70: }
71: 
72: // Begin returns the first index covered by the range (inclusive).
73: func (r *Range) Begin() uint64 {
74: 	return r.begin
75: }
76: 
77: // End returns the last index covered by the range (exclusive).
78: func (r *Range) End() uint64 {
79: 	return r.end
80: }
81: 
82: // Hashes returns sub-tree hashes corresponding to the minimal set of perfect
83: // sub-trees covering the [begin, end) range, ordered left to right.
84: func (r *Range) Hashes() [][]byte {
85: 	return r.hashes
86: }
87: 
88: // Append extends the compact range by appending the passed in hash to it. It
89: // reports all the added nodes through the visitor function (if non-nil).
90: func (r *Range) Append(hash []byte, visitor VisitFn) error {
91: 	if visitor != nil {
92: 		visitor(NewNodeID(0, r.end), hash)
93: 	}
94: 	return r.appendImpl(r.end+1, hash, nil, visitor)
95: }
96: 
97: // AppendRange extends the compact range by merging in the other compact range
98: // from the right. It uses the tree hasher to calculate hashes of newly created
99: // nodes, and reports them through the visitor function (if non-nil).
100: func (r *Range) AppendRange(other *Range, visitor VisitFn) error {
101: 	if other.f != r.f {
102: 		return errors.New("incompatible ranges")
103: 	}
104: 	if got, want := other.begin, r.end; got != want {
105: 		return fmt.Errorf("ranges are disjoint: other.begin=%d, want %d", got, want)
106: 	}
107: 	if len(other.hashes) == 0 { // The other range is empty, merging is trivial.
108: 		return nil
109: 	}
110: 	return r.appendImpl(other.end, other.hashes[0], other.hashes[1:], visitor)
111: }
112: 
113: // GetRootHash returns the root hash of the Merkle tree represented by this
114: // compact range. Requires the range to start at index 0. If the range is
115: // empty, returns nil.
116: //
117: // If visitor is not nil, it is called with all "ephemeral" nodes (i.e. the
118: // ones rooting imperfect subtrees) along the right border of the tree.
119: func (r *Range) GetRootHash(visitor VisitFn) ([]byte, error) {
120: 	if r.begin != 0 {
121: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("begin=%d, want 0", r.begin)
122: 	}
123: 	ln := len(r.hashes)
124: 	if ln == 0 {
125: 		return nil, nil
126: 	}
127: 	hash := r.hashes[ln-1]
128: 	// All non-perfect subtree hashes along the right border of the tree
129: 	// correspond to the parents of all perfect subtree nodes except the lowest
130: 	// one (therefore the loop skips it).
131: 	for i, size := ln-2, r.end; i >= 0; i-- {
132: 		hash = r.f.Hash(r.hashes[i], hash)
133: 		if visitor != nil {
134: 			size &= size - 1                              // Delete the previous node.
135: 			level := uint(bits.TrailingZeros64(size)) + 1 // Compute the parent level.
136: 			index := size >> level                        // And its horizontal index.
137: 			visitor(NewNodeID(level, index), hash)
138: 		}
139: 	}
140: 	return hash, nil
141: }
142: 
143: // Equal compares two Ranges for equality.
144: func (r *Range) Equal(other *Range) bool {
145: 	if r.f != other.f || r.begin != other.begin || r.end != other.end {
146: 		return false
147: 	}
148: 	if len(r.hashes) != len(other.hashes) {
149: 		return false
150: 	}
151: 	for i := range r.hashes {
152: 		if !bytes.Equal(r.hashes[i], other.hashes[i]) {
153: 			return false
154: 		}
155: 	}
156: 	return true
157: }
158: 
159: // appendImpl extends the compact range by merging the [r.end, end) compact
160: // range into it. The other compact range is decomposed into a seed hash and
161: // all the other hashes (possibly none). The method uses the tree hasher to
162: // calculate hashes of newly created nodes, and reports them through the
163: // visitor function (if non-nil).
164: func (r *Range) appendImpl(end uint64, seed []byte, hashes [][]byte, visitor VisitFn) error {
165: 	// Bits [low, high) of r.end encode the merge path, i.e. the sequence of node
166: 	// merges that transforms the two compact ranges into one.
167: 	low, high := getMergePath(r.begin, r.end, end)
168: 	if high < low {
169: 		high = low
170: 	}
171: 	index := r.end >> low
172: 	// Now bits [0, high-low) of index encode the merge path.
173: 
174: 	// The number of one bits in index is the number of nodes from the left range
175: 	// that will be merged, and zero bits correspond to the nodes in the right
176: 	// range. Below we make sure that both ranges have enough hashes, which can
177: 	// be false only in case the data is corrupted in some way.
178: 	ones := bits.OnesCount64(index & (1<<(high-low) - 1))
179: 	if ln := len(r.hashes); ln < ones {
180: 		return fmt.Errorf("corrupted lhs range: got %d hashes, want >= %d", ln, ones)
181: 	}
182: 	if ln, zeros := len(hashes), int(high-low)-ones; ln < zeros {
183: 		return fmt.Errorf("corrupted rhs range: got %d hashes, want >= %d", ln+1, zeros+1)
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	// Some of the trailing nodes of the left compact range, and some of the
187: 	// leading nodes of the right range, are sequentially merged with the seed,
188: 	// according to the mask. All new nodes are reported through the visitor.
189: 	idx1, idx2 := len(r.hashes), 0
190: 	for h := low; h < high; h++ {
191: 		if index&1 == 0 {
192: 			seed = r.f.Hash(seed, hashes[idx2])
193: 			idx2++
194: 		} else {
195: 			idx1--
196: 			seed = r.f.Hash(r.hashes[idx1], seed)
197: 		}
198: 		index >>= 1
199: 		if visitor != nil {
200: 			visitor(NewNodeID(h+1, index), seed)
201: 		}
202: 	}
203: 
204: 	// All nodes from both ranges that have not been merged are bundled together
205: 	// with the "merged" seed node.
206: 	r.hashes = append(append(r.hashes[:idx1], seed), hashes[idx2:]...)
207: 	r.end = end
208: 	return nil
209: }
210: 
211: // getMergePath returns the merging path between the compact range [begin, mid)
212: // and [mid, end). The path is represented as a range of bits within mid, with
213: // bit indices [low, high). A bit value of 1 on level i of mid means that the
214: // node on this level merges with the corresponding node in the left compact
215: // range, whereas 0 represents merging with the right compact range. If the
216: // path is empty then high <= low.
217: //
218: // The output is not specified if begin <= mid <= end doesn't hold, but the
219: // function never panics.
220: func getMergePath(begin, mid, end uint64) (uint, uint) {
221: 	low := bits.TrailingZeros64(mid)
222: 	high := 64
223: 	if begin != 0 {
224: 		high = bits.Len64(mid ^ (begin - 1))
225: 	}
226: 	if high2 := bits.Len64((mid - 1) ^ end); high2 < high {
227: 		high = high2
228: 	}
229: 	return uint(low), uint(high - 1)
230: }
231: 
232: // Decompose splits the [begin, end) range into a minimal number of sub-ranges,
233: // each of which is of the form [m * 2^k, (m+1) * 2^k), i.e. of length 2^k, for
234: // some integers m, k >= 0.
235: //
236: // The sequence of sizes is returned encoded as bitmasks left and right, where:
237: //   - a 1 bit in a bitmask denotes a sub-range of the corresponding size 2^k
238: //   - left mask bits in LSB-to-MSB order encode the left part of the sequence
239: //   - right mask bits in MSB-to-LSB order encode the right part
240: //
241: // The corresponding values of m are not returned (they can be calculated from
242: // begin and the sub-range sizes).
243: //
244: // For example, (begin, end) values of (0b110, 0b11101) would indicate a
245: // sequence of tree sizes: 2,8; 8,4,1.
246: //
247: // The output is not specified if begin > end, but the function never panics.
248: func Decompose(begin, end uint64) (uint64, uint64) {
249: 	// Special case, as the code below works only if begin != 0, or end < 2^63.
250: 	if begin == 0 {
251: 		return 0, end
252: 	}
253: 	xbegin := begin - 1
254: 	// Find where paths to leaves #begin-1 and #end diverge, and mask the upper
255: 	// bits away, as only the nodes strictly below this point are in the range.
256: 	d := bits.Len64(xbegin^end) - 1
257: 	mask := uint64(1)<<uint(d) - 1
258: 	// The left part of the compact range consists of all nodes strictly below
259: 	// and to the right from the path to leaf #begin-1, corresponding to zero
260: 	// bits in the masked part of begin-1. Likewise, the right part consists of
261: 	// nodes below and to the left from the path to leaf #end, corresponding to
262: 	// ones in the masked part of end.
263: 	return ^xbegin & mask, end & mask
264: }

```go
func (e Entry) LeafData(idx uint64) []byte {
	// version (1) + leaf_type (1) = MerkleTreeLeaf header
	r := []byte{0, 0}
	r = binary.BigEndian.AppendUint64(r, e.Timestamp)
	if e.IsPrecert {
		r = append(r, 1)
		r = append(r, e.IssuerKeyHash...)
		r = append(r, sizePrefix(e.RawData, 3)...)
		r = append(r, e.RawData...)
	} else {
		r = append(r, 0)
		r = append(r, sizePrefix(e.RawData, 3)...)
		r = append(r, e.RawData...)
	}
	// CtExtensions containing the leaf index
	ext := make([]byte, 8)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ext, idx)
	r = binary.BigEndian.AppendUint16(r, uint16(len(ext)))
	r = append(r, ext...)
	return r
}
```

34: // other types of transparency log would be expected to have different requirements.
35: type Storage interface {

37: 	// assigned to the entry in the log.

41: // NewCertificateTransparencySequencedWriter creates a function which can be used to submit
42: // entries to a CT log implemented using the given storage.
43: //
44: // The returned function wraps the given CT entries into the internal Entry type used by the
45: // storage, and returns the index which was assigned to each entry in the log.
46: //
47: // WARNING: This MUST ONLY be used for CT logs, and not as a basis for other transparency
48: // applications.
49: //
50: // The reasons for this are twofold:
51: //
52: //  1. The entries added to the log in this way are formatted specially (using the CT
53: //     specific format described in the ctonly package, rather than the length-prefixed
54: //     format used by other log types), and the choice of which format to use is made
55: //     at the log's storage layer, in the way that a non-CT log would not expect.
56: //
57: //  2. The Merkle leaf hash of an entry cannot be computed at the time at which it is
58: //     submitted, because the leaf data of a CT entry contains the index which will be
59: //     assigned to it, and so the hash can only be computed once the entry has been
60: //     sequenced. The storage to which entries are submitted is expected to be able to
61: //     cope with this; most notably this means that the bundle data of an entry (and so
62: //     also its Merkle leaf hash) is computed by the storage as part of sequencing the
63: //     entry, rather than by the personality.
64: func NewCertificateTransparencySequencedWriter(s Storage) func(context.Context, *ctonly.Entry) (uint64, error) {
65: 	return func(ctx context.Context, e *ctonly.Entry) (uint64, error) {
66: 		if err := e.Validate(); err != nil {
67: 			return 0, err
68: 		}

70: 		// The bundle data (and so also the Merkle leaf hash) of a CT entry depends on the
71: 		// index which will be assigned to it, so it is not possible to marshal the entry
72: 		// until it has been sequenced. The returned Entry therefore defers this marshaling
73: 		// until storage invokes MarshalBundleData with the assigned index, as part of
74: 		// sequencing.
75: 		entry := &Entry{}
76: 		entry.marshalForBundle = func(index uint64) []byte {

82: 		}

30: // data which will be stored in the log (as part of an entry bundle), and the hash of the
31: // leaf which will be used to integrate the entry into the log's Merkle tree.
32: type SequencedEntry struct {

34: 	// For most log types this is simply the data which was submitted for the entry, but for
35: 	// log types whose entry format requires it (e.g. CT), the data will have been marshaled

46: // TreeBuilder maintains the state of the log's Merkle tree and fleshes out the tiles of the
47: // tree as sequenced entries are integrated into it.
48: //
49: // Internally the tree is tracked using the compact range representation of a Merkle tree,
50: // which means that only the O(log N) hashes which comprise the "frontier" of the tree need
51: // to be kept in memory in order to compute the hashes of newly-completed nodes as entries
52: // are added.

55: // nodes of the Merkle tree at a level which is a multiple of 8 (each tile level therefore
56: // being responsible for 8 consecutive levels of the tree, with the topmost - currently
57: // incomplete - tile at each level being kept in memory until it is fully populated). On
58: // integrating a batch of entries, any tiles which become fully populated as a result are
59: // handed to the TileWriteFunc passed to Integrate, so that they can be persisted by the
60: // storage implementation.

62: // Note that TreeBuilder does not persist its own state: in the event that the process
63: // containing it is restarted, a new instance is expected to be created, and so a log is only
64: // expected to be integrated from a fresh (empty) TreeBuilder.

66: 	rf   *compact.RangeFactory
67: 	size uint64
68: 	r    *compact.Range

111: // Integrate integrates the given sequenced entries into the log's Merkle tree.
112: //
113: // Each entry's leaf hash is added to the tree; for every node of the tree whose hash
114: // becomes known as a result, the contents of the tile which the node belongs to are
115: // updated, and any tile which thereby becomes fully populated (i.e. contains its full
116: // complement of layout.LogsWidth hashes) is passed to f.
117: //
118: // On success, the returned values are the new size of the tree (i.e. the number of leaves
119: // it contains), and the root hash of the tree. If f returns an error then Integrate returns
120: // that error, along with the state of the tree at the point at which the error occurred.
121: func (t *TreeBuilder) Integrate(ctx context.Context, entries []SequencedEntry, f TileWriteFunc) (uint64, []byte, error) {
122: 	for _, e := range entries {
123: 		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
124: 			return t.size, nil, err
125: 		}
126: 		if len(e.LeafHash) != sha256.Size {
127: 			return t.size, nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid LeafHash of size %d, want %d", len(e.LeafHash), sha256.Size)
128: 		}

130: 		// Add the leaf hash to the tree, collecting the hashes of the nodes which become known
131: 		// as a result. Note that only the nodes at tree levels which are a whole number of tile
132: 		// levels above the leaves (i.e. multiples of 8) are stored as part of tiles; the hashes

134: 		// when needed, and so are not persisted.
135: 		//

137: 		// and that a tile is only persisted once it is full. This is a deliberate simplification
138: 		// which avoids the need to persist partial tiles, at the cost of possibly having to
139: 		// re-read the tile data in order to continue integrating.
140: 		var fErr error
141: 		if err := t.r.Append(e.LeafHash, func(id compact.NodeID, hash []byte) {
142: 			if id.Level%8 != 0 || fErr != nil {
143: 				return
144: 			}
145: 			fErr = t.addNode(ctx, uint8(id.Level/8), id.Index, hash, f)
146: 		}); err != nil {
147: 			return t.size, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to append leaf to tree: %v", err)
148: 		}
149: 		if fErr != nil {
150: 			return t.size, nil, fErr
151: 		}

153: 	}

155: 	if err != nil {
156: 		return 0, nil, err
157: 	}
158: 	return t.size, root, nil
159: }

173: 		return errors.New("unexpected node index: nodes for a tile level are expected to be reported contiguously")
